payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Jeanene, Layla, Mona, Pauline

payload.content:

My cheapest feasible tasks are the CRITICAL ISSUE-0002 ones (testing-tagged): review cost=7.44, test cost=10.42; implement (effort 8.0 > my 7h) cost=15.89. All ISSUE-0001 mobile-development tasks are expensive for me (16-40).

Proposal: I claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, distinct, cheap for me). Request: please don't duplicate it. Jeanene/Layla/Pauline — can two of you cover ISSUE-0002::test and ISSUE-0002::implement, and the fourth take a cheap ISSUE-0001 task (triage effort 1.6 / docs 2.0 / review 2.0)? Post your intended claims so we avoid duplicates and maximize critical coverage. I'll finalize in execution.

- ISSUE-0002 (critical, ui-ux+testing): review 7.72, test 10.81, implement 17.44 (effort 8.0 > my 6h availability → overloaded/poor fit for me)

I'm a strong testing match, so I can cover a critical ISSUE-0002 slot. Proposal to maximize critical coverage (3 criticals + 1 low = 4 tasks done):
- Mona: ISSUE-0002::review (as you proposed)
- Jeanene: ISSUE-0002::test
- Layla or Pauline (whoever has >=8h availability): ISSUE-0002::implement
- The remaining agent: a cheap ISSUE-0001 task (triage 1.6 / docs 2.0 / review 2.0)

KEY QUESTION for Layla & Pauline: what is your availability, and can either of you take ISSUE-0002::implement (needs 8h)? If implement is coverable by someone, I'll lock ISSUE-0002::test. If NOT, I'll flex to a cheap ISSUE-0001 task (e.g. triage) so we still hit 4 tasks done and avoid an overloaded claim. Please post your intended claim so we don't duplicate. I'll finalize in execution.

This yields 2 criticals + 2 lows, 4 tasks done. Compare Mona-review(7.44)+Jeanene-test(10.81)=18.25 vs my proposal Mona-test(10.42)+Layla-review(7.24)=17.66 → my proposal is cheaper by ~0.6 and also frees Jeanene for a cheap low.

QUESTION for Pauline: what is your availability? If you have >=8h, you could take ISSUE-0002::implement so we cover all 3 criticals (priority_sum 3.25 vs 2.5) — that maximizes the lexicographic objective (tasks done, then priority).

My intended claim: ISSUE-0002::review. Mona — would you flex to ::test so we minimize cost? Please post your intended claim; I'll finalize in execution.

Mona (planning, iter=1) — update. I accept the cost-minimizing flex: I will take ISSUE-0002::test (cost 10.42, the cheapest test) and let Layla take ISSUE-0002::review (7.24, cheapest review). That combo (Mona-test + Layla-review = 17.66) beats Mona-review + Jeanene-test (18.25), so it's the right call on cost.

Remaining question is ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0): it needs an agent with >=8h availability to be a clean, non-overloaded claim. None of the three of us qualify (me 7h, Jeanene 6h, Layla 4h).

Pauline — please post your availability. Two scenarios:

(B) If you have <8h: we do 2 criticals + 2 lows — Jeanene and Pauline each take a cheap ISSUE-0001 low task. 4 tasks done, priority_sum 2.5.

My intended claim: ISSUE-0002::test. Layla: ISSUE-0002::review. Jeanene: a cheap ISSUE-0001 low. Pauline: implement if >=8h, else a cheap ISSUE-0001 low. Please confirm so we lock distinct claims. I'll finalize in execution.

Rationale: I'm NOT the cheapest on any critical (test 10.81 vs Mona 10.42; review 7.72 vs Layla 7.24), so the cost-minimizing joint allocation puts me on the cheap low. My availability (6h) also can't cleanly cover implement (8.0), so I don't touch it.

Pauline — please post your availability + intended claim. Only open risk: if you (Pauline) ALSO want triage in scenario B, tell me and I'll flex to ISSUE-0001::docs (2.70) so we stay distinct. Otherwise I lock ISSUE-0001::triage in execution.

Layla (planning, iter=1) — CONFIRMED. I lock ISSUE-0002::review (cost 7.24, critical, effort 4.0 = my 4.0h availability → feasible, and I'm the cheapest on review). I cannot take ::test (5.6h) or ::implement (8.0h) since both exceed my 4h.

All four claims are distinct — no duplicates. I'll finalize with assign_task in execution.

Pauline here (planning, iter=1). Availability = 8.0h, top skill = mobile-development (0.61).

I DO have >=8h, so Scenario A is technically feasible for me — BUT my private cost for ISSUE-0002::implement is 80.00 (my fit on ui-ux-design/testing is poor; those tags aren't my skill). My ISSUE-0002 costs are: review 40.00, test 56.00, implement 80.00. My ISSUE-0001 (mobile-dev) costs are cheap: triage 2.25, review 2.82, docs 2.82, test 3.94, implement 5.63.

Joint-score check (tasks_done is 4 in both scenarios):
- Scenario A: total_cost ≈ 80.00 + 10.42 + 7.24 + 2.16 = 99.82; priority_sum = 3.25.
- Scenario B: total_cost ≈ 2.82 + 10.42 + 7.24 + 2.16 = 22.64; priority_sum = 2.50.
The extra 0.75 priority from doing implement costs ~77.2 in total_cost — that only pays off if priority_bonus > ~103, which is implausible given the defined priority weights (low 0.25 … critical 1.0). So Scenario B is the better joint-score play.

Therefore I propose Scenario B and will claim ISSUE-0001::docs (cost 2.82, low, mobile-development — my strong fit). Final distinct claims:
- Layla → ISSUE-0002::review (7.24)
- Mona → ISSUE-0002::test (10.42)
